content_of_post_to_comment: The Jubilee laws in Leviticus reset the whole economy every fifty years: debts cancelled, land returned, slaves freed. God built limits on accumulation into the law, because unchecked wealth always ends up crushing the poor. Jesus opened his ministry by announcing exactly this kind of year. The kingdom has economics, and they favour the debtor.
comment: The tension is that Jubilee challenges not just wealth accumulation but our assumptions about time: if economies need periodic resets, what does that say about systems designed around permanent debt?
